page: The Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-96 is a dedicated compute-oriented server instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 96 virtual CPUs derived from 48 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, utilizing two threads per core. System memory totals 192.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The CPU package features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a 260 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (f, vnni, bf16) as well as Intel AMX matrix extensions (amx_tile, amx_int8), providing architectural support for accelerated numerical and matrix operations. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or bundled local disk storage.

In standardized testing, the c4-highcpu-96 demonstrates top-tier multi-core compute and throughput capabilities. It registers a Geekbench multi-core score of 21998.0 and a single-core score of 2238.0. Multi-core stress-ng performance reaches 82682.91, complemented by a PassMark CPU score of 82913.7. The hardware exhibits notable throughput in data transfer and cryptography, recording a static web serving throughput of 129.97 GB/sec and a PassMark encryption score of 86639.74. Memory bandwidth testing shows cached small-block reads peaking at 6406.28 GB/sec, alongside large-block uncached read and write speeds of 298.66 GB/sec and 127.91 GB/sec. For machine learning tasks, it achieves 294.08 tokens per second on 7B model prompt processing.

Resource distribution reflects deliberate hardware tradeoffs. With 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, memory capacity is limited relative to overall processing throughput, making the instance less fitting for massive in-memory databases. Furthermore, the absence of bundled local storage means all persistent file systems must run over network-attached volumes. In terms of cost efficiency, the configuration maximizes CPU compute density, allowing workloads that scale horizontally across threads to fully utilize physical cores without paying for unneeded memory overhead. The c4-highcpu-96 fits large-scale software compilation, CPU-based machine learning inference, continuous integration pipelines, high-volume web serving, and parallel batch processing.
description: The Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-96 is a compute-focused virtual machine configured with 96 vCPUs and 192 GB of system memory. Based on the x86_64 architecture, the instance utilizes an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz across 48 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory allocation sits at 2.0 GB per vCPU, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache alongside specialized instruction sets including AMX and AVX-512. The instance contains no bundled local storage and no hardware GPUs, requiring external network block storage for persistence. Benchmark results indicate strong multi-threaded capability, achieving 82682.91 in stress-ng multi-core and 21998.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, paired with high static web throughput of 129.97 GB/sec. The machine type delivers high compute density per gigabyte of memory, making it functional for parallel batch processing, large software build pipelines, static web serving, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
